---
title: "CLI Guide"
guide-section: "Reference"
---

The per-command reference (arguments, options, `--help` text) is generated
from the Typer app and lives under **Reference → CLI**. This page covers what
the help text cannot: how the commands compose, what each one does in the VCS
and in the stores, exit codes, environment, and JSON shapes. The tutorials
([Pinning](03-pinning.qmd), [Branching and Writing](04-branching-and-writing.qmd),
[Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd)) show the same commands in
use.

```
tether init [PATH]
tether backends [--json]
tether add KEY [LOCATOR] --kind KIND [--branch BRANCH] [--at STATE | --pick] [locator options] [--set k=v]... [--file immutable|versioned] [--pin native|record] [--create]
tether set KEY... | --all [--file immutable|versioned] [--pin native|record]
tether remove KEY
tether status [--snapshot | --no-snapshot]
tether snapshot
tether pull [BOOKMARK] [-m MESSAGE]
tether commit -m MESSAGE [--no-vcs] [--strict] [--force] [--no-snapshot] [--dry-run | --plan FILE]
tether commit --from-plan FILE [-m MESSAGE] [--no-vcs]
tether new [REV] [-b NAME] [--shared] [--keep] [--eager | --lazy] [--discard] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether open KEY [-r REV] [--read-only | --writable] [--with-password]
tether restore KEY... --from REV [--discard] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether promote [KEY]... [-r REV] [--strategy auto|ff|merge] [-m MESSAGE] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether verify [-r REV] [--all-history] [--deep]
tether diff [REV_A] [REV_B] [--content] [--limit N]
tether log KEY [--ref REF] [-n N]            # or: tether log LOCATOR --kind KIND [--branch B] [--set k=v]
tether gc [--dry-run | --no-dry-run] [--release-foreign] [--prune-bookmarks [--keep-bookmark NAME]... [--force-prune]] [--delete-stores] [--store KIND=LOCATOR]... [--plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether abandon REV... [--gc]
tether drop BOOKMARK [--to BOOKMARK] [--delete-stores] [--force-prune] [--dry-run | --no-dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether forget-workspace [WORKSPACE_ID] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether ops [-n N]
tether undo [OP_ID] [--discard]
tether repair [--all-history] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether upgrade [--ignore-immutable] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
tether export PATH [--rev REV]... [--all-history | --no-all-history] [--format sqlite|parquet|csv|jsonl] [--listings] [--workspace] [--append]
tether publish [--to DSN] [--schema NAME] [--rev REV]... [--listings] [--dry-run]
tether import SOURCE [--table NAME | --query SQL] [--sync] [--dry-run | --plan FILE | --from-plan FILE]
```

Commands run from anywhere inside a dataset: the root is found by walking up
to the nearest `tether.toml`. Every command that inspects external systems
fans out concurrently across objects, and every command that prints a result
accepts `--json` except `add` and `remove`. `export`, `publish`, and `import`
are experimental and print a note saying so.

## Exit codes and errors

`0` on success, `1` on any `TetherError` (printed to stderr as `error: ...`).
`verify` also exits `1` when any report is not `ok`, `status` when any
object is `error`, and `promote` when anything was refused, which makes them
natural CI gates. `undo`, `repair`,
`upgrade`, and `forget-workspace` exit `3` when they did part of the job and
the store would not allow the rest (each such part is printed as
`IRREVERSIBLE` / `FAILED`). `2` is a usage error (an unknown option, a
missing argument), as in every Click program. Failures in one object's backend during a fan-out
are aggregated into one message listing each object.

## Revisions

`REV` arguments are passed to the enclosing VCS untouched: jj revsets (`@`,
`@-`, `main`, change ids) in a jj repository, git revisions (`HEAD~2`, tags,
shas) in a git repository. A `REV` that names a bookmark (jj) or branch (git)
is one tether works on; `tether new REV` for any other revision gives a
read-only working copy. In git that commit is checked out onto a
`tether/<rev12>` branch so the dataset commits you make there stay reachable
(a detached HEAD would let `gc` treat them as gone); those `tether/*` branches
are parking, not bookmarks -- tether never deletes them, so `git branch -d`
the ones you are done with.

## Versions and environment

tether needs **jj 0.43 or newer** (checked once per command; an older jj is
refused with the version it found) and **git 2.38 or newer** (the hardening
flags tether passes, `safe.bareRepository` among them, exist from there).

What of your own jj and git configuration reaches tether's calls: your
identity, your `.gitignore` and jj ignore rules, your hooks (a pre-commit hook
that refuses stops the dataset commit, and nothing is left staged), and jj's
`immutable_heads()`. What does not: colour, the pager, `snapshot.auto-track`
and `snapshot.max-new-file-size` (tether tracks its own files by name, and
only those), and `log.showSignature` / `core.quotePath`. Revset aliases that
shadow builtins (`all()`) do not change what tether walks: it uses operator
forms (`::`).

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `TETHER_REV` | Default `--rev` for `open`: handles resolve read-only at that commit's pinned state. Set it in reproducible jobs. |
| `PATH`, `TETHER_JJ`, `TETHER_GIT` | Which `jj` / `git` tether shells out to: `.tether/secrets.toml` `[vcs] jj_path` / `git_path`, then `TETHER_JJ` / `TETHER_GIT`, then `PATH`. Never the committed `tether.toml` (see [Configuration](08-configuration.qmd#trust-boundary-tethersecretstoml)). |
| Backend credentials | Never stored in manifests; each backend reads them from `.tether/secrets.toml` or the environment (`NEON_API_KEY`, AWS/GCP/Azure defaults, ...; Dolt only from a per-server secrets entry). See [Backends](09-backends.qmd). |
| `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_CONFIG_*`, ... | Ignored: tether clears the variables that point git at another repository or add config to it (the ones `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` lists), so running inside a git hook still commits to the repository the dataset is in. `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` are honoured. |

## Plans

`commit`, `new`, `restore`, `gc`, `drop`, `promote`, `import`, `repair`,
`upgrade`, and `forget-workspace` write to external systems (or rewrite
history), and each is a plan followed by an apply. `--dry-run` runs only the
plan and prints it (as JSON with `--json`); `--plan FILE` also saves it;
`--from-plan FILE` skips planning and applies the saved actions (so it refuses
`--dry-run` and `--plan` alongside it). Before
applying, tether re-checks the plan's preconditions -- the manifests, the
branch heads it will touch, the workspace -- and refuses with
`StalePlanError` if anything differs from what the plan recorded. `gc` and
`drop` are dry runs unless `--no-dry-run` or `--from-plan` is given. The
contract is spelled out in
[Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd#preview-before-you-write-plans).

A plan carries its own preconditions, so each command *requires* a set of
them and refuses a plan that lacks one -- saved by an older tether, or edited
-- as stale ("predates the ... precondition(s) tether now requires"). Every
plan binds to the checkout that made it (`workspace_id`, which `--plan`
persists in `workspace.toml` first) and, where it lands on or leaves a
bookmark, to that bookmark as both the workspace file and the VCS see it
(`workspace_bookmark`: git's `HEAD` branch; under jj the bookmarks at `@` or,
with edits in `@`, at `@-`):

| Command | Required preconditions | Per object |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commit` | `workspace_id`, `workspace_bookmark`, `manifest_hash` | -- |
| `new` | `workspace_id`, `manifest_hash` | each `fork`: `ref_head` (the branch exists) or `ref_absent`; each `reuse`: `ref_head` |
| `restore` | `workspace_id`, `workspace_bookmark`, `manifest_hash` | each `fork`: `ref_head` or `ref_absent` |
| `promote` | `workspace_id`, `workspace_bookmark`, `bookmark_head`, `manifest_hash` | each `fast-forward` / `merge`: `base_state`, and `ref_head` or `pin_state` |
| `drop` | `workspace_id`, `workspace_bookmark`, `bookmark_head`, `no_new_holders`, `vcs_head`, `history_digest` | -- |
| `gc`, `repair` | `workspace_id`, `history_digest` | -- |

The heads a plan reviewed are also what the stores are asked to move *from*:
`fork`, `promote` and `merge` take the expected head (or "absent") and refuse
with `RefMovedError` when the ref holds something else at the moment of the
move, so a write that lands between the check and the act is refused rather
than overwritten. Backends with a native compare-and-swap (git, Icechunk)
use it; the others compare just before acting.

```
plan: commit (2 write(s))
                 pin  zarr/imaging  [icechunk] tether.0a1b2c3d.deb4861eb388e5f6  native ref at snapshot_id=K3F9M2A1B7C8D4E5…
          vcs-commit  jj commit: 'Relabel plate1'
                      db/metrics: unchanged
```

Action verbs, by command:

| Command | Verbs |
| --- | --- |
| `commit`, `pull` | `pin`, `record`, `vcs-commit` |
| `new` | `fork`, `defer-fork`, `reuse`, `share`, `trunk` |
| `restore` | `fork`, `refuse` |
| `promote` | `fast-forward`, `merge`, `hold`, `refuse` |
| `gc` | `unpin`, `keep-pin`, `delete-branch`, `keep-branch`, `forget-working-ref`, `delete-listing`; with `--delete-stores`: `delete-store`, `keep-store`, `forget-store`, `forget-touched` |
| `drop` | `leave-bookmark`, `abandon-commit`, `delete-bookmark`, then gc's verbs |
| `forget-workspace` | `delete-file`, `forget-vcs-workspace` |
| `import` | `add`, `update`, `remove` |
| `publish` | `upsert` |
| `repair` | `repin`, `refork` |
| `upgrade` | `rename-pin`, `rename-branch`, `rewrite-history`, `rewrite-manifest`, `refingerprint`, `rename-manifest`, `rewrite-locator` |

`trunk`, `defer-fork`, `reuse`, `share`, `hold`, `refuse`, `keep-branch`,
`keep-pin`, and `keep-store` are informational -- they write nothing, and a
plan holding only those is empty.

`share` is how objects that live in one native branch space -- two databases
of a Neon project, two keys on one Icechunk store -- get *one* branch per
bookmark: the first member forks (or defers) it, the others share it, and a
member that pins a different state of the same branch is refused (a branch is
at one point; commit them together on the trunk first). `restore` and
`promote` follow the same rule: one reset or fast-forward per branch, the
siblings `share` it -- and both refuse to name only some of the objects that
write through a branch, since moving it moves them all.

## `add`, `set`, `remove`

The positional `LOCATOR` becomes the `uri` field. Named options map to locator
fields; `--set key=value` (repeatable) covers everything else. Which fields a
backend reads is listed per backend in [Backends](09-backends.qmd).

| Option | Locator field | Typical backends |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LOCATOR` (positional) | `uri` | file, icechunk, delta, lance, ducklake (`metadata`) |
| `--branch` | `branch` | icechunk, neon, iceberg, lance, dolt: the object's *upstream* (default `main`) -- what the trunk bookmark stands for: the first commit pins it, a trunk `pull` reads it, `promote` lands on it |
| `--project-id`, `--database`, `--role` | same | neon; `--database` also dolt |
| `--remote` | `remote` | git (push pins to a remote) |
| `--region` | `region` | file (object stores), icechunk, delta |
| `--host`, `--port` | same | dolt |
| `--table` | `table` | ducklake (handle scope), iceberg (alias of `identifier`) |
| `--at ID` / `--pick` | `at` | initial position: snapshot id / version / commit / tag (all but file, neon) that the first commit pins instead of the branch head; `--pick` chooses from `log` interactively |
| `--set k=v` | `k` | `path=`, `identifier=`, `data_path=`, `allow_dirty=1`, ... |
| `--create` | -- | **experimental**: make an empty store at the locator first (`CREATE` backends: icechunk, git, a local `file` directory), mark it as this dataset's, and index it so `gc --delete-stores` can delete it once nothing references it. Refused if anything already exists there. On a bookmark the store's working branch is forked at once. From Python, `repo.create(key, kind, locator)` does this and opens the handle. |

Policy options: `--file immutable|versioned` (`file` only: treat drift as an
error, or record object-store version ids) and `--pin native|record` (any
backend: create a native ref per commit, or record the state only and fork
from it while the system retains it -- see
[Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd)). `tether set KEY... --file|--pin`
changes a registered object's policy in place (`--all` for every object):
manifest-only, logged, undoable; commit to record it. Whether writes fork or
land upstream is not a policy: it is the bookmark the working copy is on.

`tether remove KEY` deletes the manifest and nothing else: the object's
working ref stays in `.tether/workspace.toml` until a plain `gc` forgets it,
and the store branch itself is judged by the next `gc --prune-bookmarks` like
any other stray.

## `status`

```
dataset 3f9c2a1b7d0e (STALE: zarr/imaging); on bookmark relabel
       new  raw/plate1  [file/observed] unrecoverable
  modified  zarr/imaging  [icechunk/forkable]
     clean  db/metrics  [neon/forkable] verify=ok
```

- The header names the bookmark this working copy is on (`on trunk bookmark
  main`; `on no bookmark: read-only`), and a `warning:` line follows when the
  VCS moved, renamed, or deleted it behind tether's back, with what to do.
- States: `new` (no commit yet), `modified` (the bookmark's branch for the
  object differs from the commit), `behind` (on the trunk, a branch-less or
  `--at` object whose system moved past its pin -- `pull` takes it), `clean`,
  `error` (the fingerprint failed: the other objects are still reported, the
  reason follows on stderr, and `status` exits `1`).
- `unrecoverable`: the committed state cannot be reconstructed later
  (Observed).
- `(created)`: the store was made by `add --create` (`origin = "created"` in
  the manifest; informational -- `gc` decides deletion from the store's owner
  marker, not from this).
- `(STALE)`: HEAD's manifests changed since this workspace forked its refs;
  the objects are named, and writable `open` and `commit` refuse for all until
  `tether new`.
- `verify=`: shown when `[verify] on_status = true`.

`status` is local by default: it shows the *last* snapshot of each object's
state and prints its age (`states as fingerprinted 2h ago; --snapshot to
refresh`), contacting nothing -- like `jj status`, it is meant to be cheap
enough to run constantly. `--snapshot` fans out and fingerprints every object
first: one metadata round-trip per system in parallel, so wall time is the
slowest one (a suspended Neon compute has to wake). A workspace with no
snapshot yet always takes one. `[snapshot] auto = true` makes every `status`
fingerprint; `--no-snapshot` then wins. `verify` always fingerprints. A commit
refreshes the cache only for the objects it fingerprinted, so an object a
fan-out found `behind` still reads `behind` after an unrelated commit. See
[Positions](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#positions-and-tether-pull).

## `commit`

1. Refuse if the VCS working copy has left the bookmark (`status` says how to
   return). Under jj the bookmark must be on the working copy or its parent
   -- where `new` and `commit` leave it; a `jj new` past an empty change puts
   it a step further back, and `commit` refuses rather than move it in a
   second operation (`tether new NAME --keep` brings the working copy back
   without touching branches). Snapshot the bookmark's branches -- on the
   trunk every upstream branch, elsewhere the `tether.ws.*` branches that
   exist -- unless `--no-snapshot`. Objects with no branch keep their pin.
   Then quiescence checks for backends that need them (Neon refuses while
   writers are active; `--force` skips).
2. For each object whose state changed: Pinnable/Forkable backends create the
   native ref `tether.<pin_id>`; Addressable and `--pin record` objects record
   the state; Observed backends record it with `recoverable = false`
   (`--strict` fails instead). Unchanged objects are skipped. If a pin fails,
   pins created by the same commit are released best-effort.
3. Write `.tether/objects/<key>.toml` and any `.tether/listings/<hash>.jsonl`,
   then `jj commit` / `git commit` scoped to those paths (`--no-vcs` skips).
4. Move the bookmark onto the new commit (one jj operation with the commit,
   so `jj undo` takes both back; git branches follow by themselves). The
   store branches stay where they are: `commit` is not `jj commit`, nothing
   new is forked, and the next write lands on the same branch.

## `pull`

The dataset's fetch. For the bookmark this working copy is on (the only one
it can pull; `tether new NAME` first for another): fingerprint the heads of
its branches -- on the trunk, every object's upstream branch (`locator.branch`,
ignoring `at`) and, for systems without branches, the object itself; on any
other bookmark, its `tether.ws.*` branches -- and, where that differs from the
bookmark's commit, pin it and commit on the bookmark, which moves. Nothing
moved: no commit. Objects not yet committed, and objects whose branch does not
exist yet, are skipped with a reason; a `file = "immutable"` object that
changed is refused; uncommitted manifest edits are refused (commit them
first). `undo` uncommits a pull like a commit.

## `new`

Decides which bookmark this working copy works on, then records a working ref
per Forkable object. `-b NAME` creates the bookmark at `REV` (default: here)
-- refused if it exists; `REV` naming a bookmark joins it; any other `REV`
takes the bookmark at that commit (the one this workspace has, else the
trunk, else the only one) or, if none, makes the working copy read-only; no
`REV` keeps the current bookmark. A bookmark another live checkout works on is
refused unless `--shared`. On the trunk (`[vcs] trunk`, default `main`) the
working ref is each object's upstream branch (`trunk` in the plan); on any
other bookmark it is `tether.ws.<dataset>.<bookmark>` in that object's system.
By default (`[new] fork = "lazy"`) that branch is *not created yet* -- the plan
shows `defer-fork` and the first writable `open` creates it from the pin.
`--eager` creates them all during `new`. Objects with `pin = "record"` fork
during `new` regardless, because only a branch keeps their recorded state from
expiring. `Repo.materialize_fork(key)` creates one deferred branch on demand.
The trade-offs: [Lazy or eager](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#lazy-or-eager).

A working branch this workspace already has is *reset* onto the pin by the
fork -- unless it already sits exactly at the pin (you just committed from
it), in which case the plan says `reuse` and the branch is kept as is. If its
head holds writes that were never committed, the plan shows a `refuse` action
and `new` stops before touching the VCS or any store; commit the writes, or
pass `--discard` to throw them away (the fork action then says what it
discards).

## `open`

| Handle | Address |
| --- | --- |
| `FileHandle` | `uri[#version_id]` |
| `NeonHandle` | connection URL, password redacted (`--with-password` prints it; `--json` never does) |
| `GitHandle` | `path@sha` |
| `IcechunkHandle` | `uri#<tag or branch or snapshot_id>` |
| `IcebergHandle` | `identifier#<ref or snapshot_id>` |
| `DeltaHandle` | `uri@vN` |
| `LanceHandle` | `uri#tag` or `uri#branch@vN` |
| `DuckLakeHandle` | `metadata#snapshot=N` |
| `DoltHandle` | `mysql://user@host:port/db/ref` |

Without `-r` (and without `TETHER_REV`), Forkable objects open **writable** at
their working ref -- creating it first if `new` deferred the fork, the one
store write that is not its own command -- and everything else read-only at
the base. With `-r REV`, the handle is read-only at that commit's pinned (or
recorded Addressable) state.

## `restore`

`tether restore KEY... --from REV` is the per-object `jj restore --from`: it
resets (or creates) `KEY`'s working branch from what `REV`'s manifest pinned
and touches nothing else -- other objects' branches, the working-tree
manifests, and the VCS working copy stay. The object is *not* stale
afterwards: the next `commit` pins what you restored. Its fork point moves to
`REV`'s state, so `promote` treats a base that moved since as a divergence
(merge or refuse), not a fast-forward. Whether the branch exists, and what it
holds, is the store's answer, not the workspace's: a fork `new` deferred may
have been created since by a `--shared` peer, and a branch holding writes
nobody committed is refused unless `--discard` (a head that cannot be read is
refused outright). The plan binds to each head it reviewed, so a write in
between makes it stale. `undo` of a restore deletes the branch if the restore
*created* it and otherwise reports the head it had: `restore` again, from the
commit you want, is the way back.

## `promote`

Per Forkable object, compares the upstream branch to the fork point recorded
when the bookmark's branch was created (or, with `--rev`, to the target's
ancestry): unchanged and `PROMOTE` -> `fast-forward`; moved and `MERGE` ->
`merge`; otherwise `refuse` with the backend's recipe. `--strategy ff` turns
merges into refusals, `--strategy merge` turns fast-forwards into refusals.

What lands is what the bookmark's commit records: a working branch with
writes since the last commit is refused (`tether commit` them first), because
the trunk moves to that commit and its manifest must describe the upstream.

A bookmark is planned whole or not at all: if any object is refused and no
keys were named, the others are `held` (the output says what each would have
done) and nothing is written -- a refusal never leaves `main` with a mix of
landed and unlanded systems. At apply the merges run first and the
fast-forwards only once every merge landed: a merge is what can still stop
(a conflict, a base that moved), and a fast-forward cannot be taken back.
Beyond that each system's move stands on its own, so a backend that fails
mid-apply leaves the systems before it landed and the trunk bookmark where it
was (`promote` again finishes the rest; there is no cross-system undo).
`tether promote KEY...` lands a subset on purpose; the trunk bookmark never
moves for a subset. When everything fast-forwarded and nothing was refused,
the trunk bookmark is moved to the commit the plan reviewed (`main ->
<commit>` in the output) -- the bookmark's commit at plan time, not wherever
the checkout is by the time the plan is applied. After a merge the branch is
reset onto the merge result so the next `commit` pins it (a branch that
gained writes during the merge is left as it is and named in the output),
and a second `promote` -- with every base already at what that commit records
-- moves the trunk. Exit status is `1` when anything was refused (conflicts
included). The walkthrough: [Landing it](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#landing-it-tether-promote).

## `drop`

`tether drop BOOKMARK` throws a bookmark away: the opposite of `promote`, in
one step. Dry-run by default; the plan lists, in order:

1. `leave-bookmark` -- when this checkout is on it, `new` to `--to` (default
   the trunk) first. A bookmark another live checkout works on is refused.
2. `abandon-commit`, one per commit that only this bookmark reaches. Commits
   another bookmark also reaches stay, so a line that branched off this one
   keeps its base. (jj: `jj abandon`; git: nothing reaches them once the
   branch is gone.)
3. `delete-bookmark`.
4. the store side: `gc --prune-bookmarks` restricted to this bookmark's
   branches, the pins nothing references once the commits are gone, and with
   `--delete-stores` the experimental created-store step. One rule is
   `drop`'s own: a branch whose head a *dropped commit* pinned or recorded is
   deleted -- that is committed work you are throwing away by name -- where
   `gc` alone would keep it as "unpinned writes". Writes no commit ever
   recorded are still kept unless `--force-prune`.

The store actions in the plan are a preview computed as if the commits were
already gone; apply re-plans them live after the VCS half, because `gc`
binds to the history it sees. The plan is stale -- refused with "re-run the
plan" -- if it is applied in another checkout, the bookmark moved, this
checkout moved (to another commit, or onto or off the bookmark), history
changed, another checkout started working on the bookmark, or the set of
commits only the
bookmark reaches changed (a `promote` or a `jj bookmark set` onto the line in
between); that last one is re-derived at apply, never trusted from a saved
plan. Refused for the trunk. "Only the bookmark reaches" is exact: another
bookmark, a tag, a remote bookmark (`feature@origin`, `origin/feature`) or
another workspace's working copy on the line all keep the commits, and the
plan then deletes just the bookmark and notes what still reaches them (jj:
the next `jj git push` deletes the remote side; git: `git push <remote>
--delete feature`).

Not undoable by tether, and a `drop` you regret is three steps, in order and
before the next `gc`:

1. `jj undo` (jj) or `git branch feature <sha>` from `git reflog` (git):
   the commits and the bookmark are back.
2. `tether repair --all-history`: it re-pins what those commits recorded
   (`--all-history` because this checkout is not on them yet). Their states
   are still in the stores if nothing has cleaned them -- an Icechunk
   snapshot is only unreachable, not deleted, until the repository's own
   expiry runs.
3. `tether new feature` to work on it again. The `tether.ws.*` branches
   `drop` deleted are gone; the bookmark starts from its pins, as a fresh
   fork.

## `abandon`

`tether abandon REV...` is the surgical form: `jj abandon` / a git rebase
that drops the named commits from a line you keep, plus the `gc` plan for the
pins only they referenced. Later commits keep their manifests exactly as they
were (snapshot, not patch, semantics -- the VCS's own rebase would conflict on
them). Nothing is released unless `--gc`; `tether gc --no-dry-run` does it
later. Under git the commits must be on the current branch and the tree
clean; a conflict outside `.tether/` aborts. Not undoable by tether -- `jj
undo` / the reflog bring the commits back, `repair` the pins. To throw a whole
bookmark away, use `drop`.

## `gc`

Default: release pins no manifest references -- in VCS history (every side
of a conflicted jj commit included), in this working tree, or in any other
live checkout's -- and that no operation still running or interrupted made;
forget the working refs of objects removed with `tether remove` (the native
branch is left alone); and delete unreferenced `.tether/listings/` files. No
branch is ever deleted by a plain `gc`.

Only pins **this clone created** are released. The store is shared by every
clone of the dataset and pins are content-addressed, so an unreferenced pin
may be another clone's, made by commits you have not fetched; such a pin is
kept and listed as `keep-pin` (`not created by this clone`). Fetch, or pass
`--release-foreign` to release them too. Which pins are this clone's is
recorded in `tether-pinned.jsonl` beside the repository lock (`.jj/repo/` or
`.git/`), seeded from the op logs the first time it is needed.

`gc` (and `drop`) refuse while jj reports a conflicted bookmark or commit:
resolve it (`jj bookmark set`, `jj resolve`) first.

`--prune-bookmarks` also sweeps `tether.ws.*` branches: those of bookmarks
that are gone (every bookmark the VCS has, or a live checkout works on, is
kept; `--keep-bookmark NAME` keeps one that only exists elsewhere), legacy
per-workspace branches from before bookmarks, and this bookmark's branches
that no current object uses. Each branch gets one verdict:

| Branch head | Default | `--force-prune` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| natively pinned by some commit, or equal to the base branch | `delete-branch` | `delete-branch` |
| holds unpinned writes | `keep-branch` | `delete-branch FORCED` (data lost) |
| a `--pin record` state (no native ref) | `keep-branch` | `delete-branch FORCED` |
| on a `BRANCH_IS_STORAGE` backend (Neon) | `keep-branch` | `delete-branch FORCED` |
| the store refuses to delete it (Neon: pins hang off it) | `keep-branch: cannot be deleted` | same |

Both sweeps stay inside this dataset's namespace: pins and branches whose
name carries another dataset's id are counted in the plan's notes (`N pin(s)
of other datasets left alone`) and never touched, `--force-prune` included.

`--delete-stores` (opt-in, **experimental** -- the command says so) adds a
last step for stores this dataset *created* (`add --create`) that no manifest
in history or in any live checkout's working tree names any more. Their pins
are unpinned and their branches judged by the table above (without
`--prune-bookmarks` a branch blocks the store), and then:

| The store | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| owner marker names this dataset; every branch belongs to a bookmark this clone had; nothing left but the base branch at its initial state, the refs this plan deletes, and no uncommitted files | `delete-store` (always the last action; `store_empty` precondition) |
| a same-dataset branch of a bookmark this clone never had, or a same-dataset pin no commit of this clone made (another actor may be working there) | `keep-store`; nothing in the store is touched (`--force-prune` overrides) |
| a branch or pin of another dataset, writes on the base branch, a branch of ours that is kept, or a backend that cannot tell | `keep-store: <what remains>` |
| marker names another dataset | note; left alone |
| no marker (removed by hand, or taken over) | `forget-store`: dropped from the index |

`--store KIND=LOCATOR` (repeatable) adds a created store to consider even when
this clone's index does not have it -- the creator's clone is gone -- under the
same rules; it implies `--delete-stores`. Under the same flag, `gc` also looks
inside the stores this clone has *touched* (forked a branch in, or pinned --
`tether-touched.jsonl`) that no manifest names any more, and releases this
dataset's dead refs there; a store with nothing of the dataset's left is
dropped from that index (`forget-touched`). `undo gc` reports a deleted store
as irreversible. The rules in full:
[Stores tether created](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd#stores-tether-created).

## `forget-workspace`

`tether forget-workspace [ID]` (default: this one) is `jj workspace forget` /
`git worktree remove` plus tether's half: its `workspace.toml` and `ops.jsonl`
are removed and the VCS stops tracking the checkout. Store branches belong to
bookmarks, not workspaces, so none are touched -- `jj bookmark delete NAME`
then `gc --prune-bookmarks` (or `tether drop NAME`) releases them. Forgetting
the current workspace leaves the directory without a working copy under jj,
as `jj workspace forget` does. Plan/apply; not undoable. The retire-a-bookmark
flow: [Branches of bookmarks that are gone](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd#branches-of-bookmarks-that-are-gone).

## `ops`, `undo`, `repair`

### The operation log

The VCS records the manifests. It cannot see which native refs `commit`
created, which branches `new` forked or reset and what their heads were
before, what `gc` deleted, or where `promote` moved a base branch from. Every
apply therefore writes an entry to `.tether/ops.jsonl` -- per workspace,
untracked, append-only, like jj's own `op log` -- holding the plan it applied,
what it did, and what it replaced. `tether ops` prints the newest entries,
one line each: id, time, command, what it did, and `(undone by ID)` where
applicable.

The log is a journal: a store-writing command appends its entry (plan and
what `undo` would need) and syncs it *before* the first side effect, then
appends a completion mark with the result. A process killed in between leaves
an entry marked `INCOMPLETE`; `undo` refuses it (what it did is not known),
`repair --dry-run` names it, and `gc` collects whatever it left. The `new`
and `gc` a `drop` runs are journaled as its steps (`parent` in the JSON,
`(step of ID)` in the listing). Each side
effect also appends a progress record as it takes effect, so `repair
--dry-run` can say which forks, unpins, or fast-forwards of an interrupted
operation had already happened; running the command again finishes what is
left.

One writer holds `.tether/lock` for the duration of a writing command, so two
`tether` processes in one checkout cannot interleave journal entries and
`workspace.toml` writes (threads sharing one `Repo` take turns the same way).
Commands that create references to pins (`commit`, `pull`), release them
(`gc`), remove commits (`undo`, `abandon`, `drop`), or create a bookmark's
store branch (`new`, the first writable `open` on a `--shared` bookmark) also
hold a repository-wide lock in the VCS's shared directory, so a gc here cannot
race a commit in another workspace, and two `--shared` checkouts cannot both
find a branch absent and fork over each other. Where the platform has no
`fcntl` (Windows) writing commands are refused; see
[Caveats](12-caveats-and-performance.qmd#one-writer-per-checkout-one-per-repository).

`commit` compensates as a unit: if anything fails after the pins -- a
manifest write, a listing, the VCS commit -- the pins this commit created are
released (never a pin an earlier commit made and this one merely reused), the
manifests it wrote are put back, and the journal records the attempt as
failed and rolled back. The one thing it never undoes is a dataset commit that
landed: if the adapter fails *after* writing the commit, history already names
the pins, so the operation completes as a commit that succeeded and the
trailing error is reported.

### `undo`

`tether undo [OP_ID]` reverses the newest entry (or the one named) *where the
store still allows it*, and says exactly what it could not reverse. Undos and
what they reversed are skipped, so several slips in a row are several `undo`s;
anything else the newest entry cannot be -- a `drop`, an `INCOMPLETE`
operation -- is refused, not skipped: undoing the `new` before a `drop` would
bring back half of what the drop threw away. Name an older entry by id and
only the `workspace.toml` fields *that* entry changed come back, never what
later entries did to the rest.

```
$ tether undo
undid 3f1c9a2b7d4e (new: forked db, zarr/imaging)
  restored   db: deleted tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel
  restored   zarr/imaging: deleted tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.relabel
  restored   workspace.toml restored
```

| Undoing a... | Does | Refused when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commit` | uncommits it (jj: squash into `@`; git: `reset --soft`); manifests become working-tree edits; pins stay | it is no longer the working copy's parent; under jj, other commits are built on it (squashing it away would rewrite them -- `jj backout` instead) |
| `new`, lazy fork, `restore` | deletes the branches it *created*, restores the `workspace.toml` fields it changed, returns the VCS working copy if it has not moved, deletes a bookmark `-b` made; a branch it *reset* is reported with its old head (`IRREVERSIBLE`, exit `3`) -- `restore KEY --from REV` or `new --discard` puts it where you want | a created branch gained writes since, or holds a state a manifest records with no pin of its own (a `pin = "record"` object committed on it): commit or undo those, or `--discard` |
| `pull` | uncommits it like a `commit`; pins stay | it is no longer the working copy's parent |
| `gc` | restores forgotten working refs and deleted listings; deleted *branches* and *pins* stay deleted and print as `IRREVERSIBLE` (exit `3`) -- `repair` recreates a bookmark's branches from its manifests, and pins while the state is reachable | -- |
| `add`, `remove`, `set`, `import` | restores the manifests (and `undo add` removes a store `--create` made while it is still empty) | -- |
| `promote` | -- | always; the previous upstream heads are printed (the trunk bookmark: `jj bookmark set main -r <before>`) |
| `repair`, `upgrade`, `abandon`, `drop`, `forget-workspace` | -- | always |
| the `new` or `gc` a `drop` ran | -- | always: they are steps of the drop (`tether ops` shows them under it), undone with it or not at all -- `jj undo` brings the commits and bookmark back, `repair` the branches and pins |

The rule for the store side: `undo` deletes what an operation *created* and
never guesses where something it *reset* should go -- that is a `restore` you
choose. Several slips in a row are several `undo`s, newest first (there is no
`jj op restore` equivalent: tether's log holds per-operation deltas, not whole
views). A created branch that gained writes since the operation is never
deleted silently: `undo` refuses until you commit them or pass `--discard`.

When the VCS goes around tether (`jj undo`, `jj abandon`, `git reset` on a
dataset commit), `tether status` prints a `warning:` per vanished commit and
`tether ops` flags its entry `(vcs commit gone)`. An *undone* commit leaves the
manifests as uncommitted edits -- commit again; an *abandoned* one reverts
them -- `gc` releases its pins, `repair` recreates them if it comes back.
`jj undo` and `git reset` revert the manifests, never the stores: use them for
the VCS side, `tether undo` for tether's.

### `repair`

`tether repair` is the other direction: given the manifests, rebuild what
they promise. A pin whose native ref is gone is recreated from the recorded
state (as long as the store still has it); a working branch this workspace
expects but the store lost is forked again. `--all-history` checks every
commit's pins, not just the working tree's. Pins that exist but point
elsewhere are reported as notes, never overwritten. Plan/apply like the
others.

Icechunk keeps a tombstone for every deleted tag and never lets the name be
reused, so there a repinned pin lives under the next *generation* of its id
(`tether.<id>.2`, `.3`, ...). The pin id and the manifests do not change;
`verify` reports `ok  pinned as tether.<id>.2`, and every reader resolves a
pin through its live generation. Until the repair, `open --rev` and `new`
fall back to the recorded snapshot while the store has it.

## `upgrade`

`tether.toml` carries `[tether] version`. A dataset made by an older tether is
refused by every command except `upgrade` (and the error says so). One
migration brings any alpha dataset to the current version: its parts run on
what the dataset *shows* (old-format pins, mtime file states, misplaced
manifests), not on the version it recorded, the version is written once at
the end, and one VCS commit lands it. An interrupted upgrade re-runs the same
plan; the store renames already made are skipped.

::: {.callout-warning title="Removed at 0.1.0"}
The alpha upgrade path lives in `tether.upgrade` and ships with the 0.1.0
betas only. The first non-pre-release drops it: a dataset at an alpha version
then fails at open with a message naming the last beta. To bring an alpha
dataset forward after that, `pip install "tether-vcs==0.1.0b3"` (or the
newest beta), run `tether upgrade` there, and reinstall the release. Datasets
already at the current version are unaffected.
:::

```
$ tether upgrade --dry-run
plan: upgrade (5 write(s))
          rename-pin  db  [icechunk] tether.0a1b2c3d.7d1e0c9a2b34e5f6  from tether.7d1e0c9a2b34
          rename-pin  db  [icechunk] tether.0a1b2c3d.c48b2f6e1d07a9b0  from tether.c48b2f6e1d07
       rename-branch  db  [icechunk] tether.ws.0a1b2c3d.7c1e0a4d.db-61a22c  from tether.ws.7c1e0a4d.db
     rewrite-history      3 commit(s)  manifests with old-format pins get the new names; commit ids change, every clone must re-sync
          vcs-commit      tether upgrade: v1 -> v4
                          dataset id: 0a1b2c3d
```

| Migration | Parts (each only when the dataset shows the condition) | Touches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any alpha version -> v4 | **dataset-namespaced refs**: dataset id; every pin and working branch renamed into its namespace (the branches keep their pre-bookmark per-workspace names, which `gc --prune-bookmarks` judges as legacy). **content-hashed file states; no write policy**: local `file` states become content hashes (one read per file; the stat cache remembers); the `write` policy line is dropped -- whether writes fork or land upstream is the bookmark now; a workspace with no bookmark adopts the trunk. **one manifest file per key; absolute local paths**: `.toml` is appended to the key's last segment (`foo.bar` -> `foo.bar.toml`; before, `foo` and `foo.bar` shared `foo.toml`); relative local paths in locators are resolved against the dataset root | stores and history (first part); working tree only (the others) |

The part that renames native refs has to rewrite history too: `gc`
subtracts what history references from what the stores hold, and both sides
must agree. That means:

- Commit ids change (jj keeps change ids; bookmarks and branches follow).
  Every other clone re-syncs afterwards: `jj git fetch`, or a force-push and
  reset under git.
- Under jj, commits marked immutable (pushed `main`) are only rewritten with
  `--ignore-immutable`.
- It fails **closed**: the dataset id is written first, then the store
  renames; the first failed rename stops the upgrade with history and
  manifests still naming the old refs, so nothing is orphaned.
- Re-running `tether upgrade` continues under the same id and skips the
  renames already made.

## `log`

Lists an object's native history newest first: id, timestamp, message, and
the branches, tags, and tether pins (`tether.<id>`) pointing at each entry.
For a registered object it starts at the working ref (or the `at` it was
registered at); `--ref` starts elsewhere (a branch, tag, or id). With `--kind`,
the positional is a locator for an unregistered object, so you can browse
before `add`. Ids are valid `--at` values.

## `diff`

No arguments: the last commit (`HEAD` in git, `@-` in jj) vs working tree. One revision: that revision vs
nothing (everything `removed`). Two: `REV_A → REV_B`. `--content` adds each
changed object's native diff; `--limit` caps entries printed per object
(counts stay exact).

## `export`, `publish`, `import`

The registry commands are covered in [Registries and SQL](10-registries-and-sql.qmd).
In short: `export` writes the derived tables to a SQLite file (default) or a
directory of parquet / csv / jsonl files; `publish` upserts them into a
Postgres schema (DSN from `--to` or `$TETHER_PUBLISH_DSN`, never
`tether.toml`) and skips commits already present; `import` reads rows with the
canonical object columns from a Postgres DSN, SQLite file, `.csv`, or `.jsonl`
and plans `add` / `update` / `remove` (`--sync`) on the manifests. `import` is
a planned command like `commit`, `new`, and `gc`; `publish --dry-run` prints
per-table counts.

## JSON output

| Command | Shape |
| --- | --- |
| `init` | `{"root": "<absolute path>", "dataset_id": "<8 hex>"}` |
| `backends` | `[{"kind", "installed", "maturity", "tier", "capabilities": [names]}]` (an uninstalled extra: `installed` false, the rest null) |
| `status` | `{"manifest_hash", "stale", "stale_keys", "fresh", "snapshot_at", "bookmark", "trunk", "bookmark_drift": [str], "vcs_drift": [{"op", "commit", "referenced": {key: bool}}], "objects": [{"key", "kind", "tier", "state", "pinned", "recoverable", "origin", "verify", "error": str or null}]}`; `fresh` is false when the cached snapshot from `snapshot_at` was shown |
| `set` | `{"changed": {key: {field: {"from", "to"}}}, "unchanged": [keys]}` |
| `pull` | `{"bookmark", "committed": {key: {"from", "to"}}, "unchanged": [keys], "skipped": [keys], "vcs_commit", "pinned": {key: pin_id or null}}` |
| `snapshot` | `{key: state}` |
| `commit` | `{"vcs_commit": sha or null, "pinned": {key: ref or null}, "unrecoverable": [keys], "unchanged": [keys]}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan (below) |
| `new` | `{"bookmark", "working_refs": {key: ref}, "pending_forks": {key: ref}, "fork_points": {key: state}}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `promote` | `{"fast_forwarded": {key: state}, "merged": {key: state}, "skipped": [keys], "refused": {key: reason}, "held": {key: reason}, "conflicts": {key: [units]}, "trunk_moved": commit or null, "trunk_held": reason or null}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `open` | `{"key", "read_only", "address", "type"}` |
| `restore` | `{"from": rev, "working_refs": {key: ref}}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `verify` | `{label: {"status", "message"}}` with labels `key` or `<commit12>:key` |
| `diff` | `[{"key", "change", "a": pin_id or null, "b": pin_id or null, "detail": ObjectDiff or null, "detail_error": str or null}]` where `ObjectDiff` is `{"summary", "unit", "added", "removed", "modified", "truncated", "note", "entries": [{"path", "change", "detail"}]}` |
| `log` | `[{"id", "when", "message", "refs": [names]}]` |
| `gc` | dry run (default): the plan; after applying: `{"dry_run": false, "unpinned": {kind: [pin_ids]}, "deleted_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "kept_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "forgotten_working_refs": {key: [refs]}, "deleted_listings": [names], "deleted_stores": {key: where}, "kept_stores": {key: reason}, "forgotten_stores": [keys]}` |
| `abandon` | `{"abandoned": [commit ids], "gc_plan": plan, "gc_applied": bool}` |
| `drop` | `{"bookmark", "left_for": bookmark or null, "abandoned": [commit ids], "gc": {the applied gc's fields} or null}`; dry run (default): the plan |
| `forget-workspace` | `{"workspace": id8, "removed_files": [paths], "vcs": str or null, "failed": {target: reason}}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `ops` | `[{"id", "at", "command", "plan", "result", "pre", "undoes", "undone_by", "status", "parent", "progress", "vcs_commit_gone"}]`, newest first; `parent` names the `drop` an entry is a step of |
| `undo` | `{"undone": op id, "command", "undo_id", "restored": [str], "irreversible": [str], "skipped": [str]}` |
| `repair` | `{"repinned": {key: pin_id}, "reforked": {key: ref}, "failed": {target: reason}, "notes": [str]}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| `upgrade` | `{"from_version", "to_version", "renamed_pins": {old ref: new ref}, "renamed_branches": {old: new}, "rewritten_commits": {old id: new id}, "refingerprinted": [keys], "rewritten_manifests": [keys], "failed": {target: reason}, "vcs_commit"}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
| plan | `{"format": 2, "command", "created_at", "context": {...}, "notes": [str], "preconditions": [{"kind", "expected", "key", "params": {...}, "detail"}], "actions": [{"op", "key", "kind", "target", "detail", "params": {...}}]}` -- what `--plan FILE` writes and `--from-plan` reads; precondition kinds are `tether.plan.PRECONDITION_KINDS`, and a format-1 plan is refused |
| `export` | `{"path", "format", "head", "rows": {table: count}}` |
| `publish` | `{"schema", "head", "upserted": {table: count}, "skipped_commits"}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan (one `upsert` action per table) |
| `import` | `{"added": [keys], "updated": [keys], "removed": [keys], "unchanged": [keys]}`; with `--dry-run`: the plan |
